description: Two more of the 35 targeted PROP IDs name call sites that do not exist in the current implementation, independently of FIND-001/002's funding-gate root cause. (1) PROP-201a: 'A gen-wallet.sh output whose address derives from the documented sha256-fallback path... is detected and rejected, never used', verification method 'assert the caller aborts rather than proceeding with the fallback address.' REQ-201's own EARS clause (behavioral-spec.md line ~1697) makes this a hard SHALL: 'SHALL verify the resulting address is a real keccak256-derived Ethereum address... and abort the spawn attempt' -- not merely documentation. spawn-orchestrator.mjs's actual defaultGenerateEvmWallet() (lines 118-122) does `JSON.parse(out)` and returns `{address, privateKey}` with zero validation of any kind -- no keccak/sha256-fallback detection, no abort logic, no cross-check re-derivation. This 'caller aborts' mechanism PROP-201a names simply does not exist. (2) PROP-302c: a post-RUNNING 'nosana job ssh <job> [port]' secrets-injection call site. grep of spawn-orchestrator.mjs for 'nosana'/'Nosana' (case-insensitive) finds only a code comment admitting 'no Nosana deploy path exist[s] anywhere in this codebase yet' (line 131-134), a hardcoded `nosanaAvailable: false` in defaultSelectCloudTarget (line 136), and an error string listing 'nosana' as an option that never resolves true. defaultDeploy() (lines 139-151) rejects any target other than the literal string "akash". No 'nosana job ssh' invocation, nor any Nosana deploy invocation of any kind, exists anywhere in the current implementation.

evidence.testName: grep -inE "keccak|fallback|validate|crossCheck" skills/self/spawn/lib/spawn-orchestrator.mjs -> no matches; grep -in "nosana" skills/self/spawn/lib/spawn-orchestrator.mjs -> only the 3 lines quoted above, no invocation
